column1: # The routes and what must hold on each replay: tools/check_routes.py (ctest oracles-routes, with ORACLES_ROM_DIR set).

# Link's sprite as drawn goes back on the screen three times in overworld.route (enhanced.link_backsteps_y): the camera's catch-up stepping on a frame his sprite does not, and twice his jump off a ledge, his height drawn while the camera follows the ground; and once across (enhanced.link_backsteps), at 3722, the scroll down from 0:c6 into 0:d6 loading: the frames of the load show the sprite the game drew before it, a pixel short of his place the camera catches up on.
# overworld.route in the far view fitted to the screen (--screen): 426x320 on 1280x960, 412x360 on 1240x1080, the rules of its far 4:3 rows.
# overworld.route in the view's other sizes (docs/PLAYING.md): near in 4:3, medium in 16:9 and 4:3.

# overworld.route in the far view with the status bar full width: the houses' loads keep the band as in play; the play area moves once, at the end of the first load, where Link walks out of his house into a room the camera only frames once he is in it.

# On mGBA, continuous-transitions.route parts from its recording: at frame 6611 the game's logic on mGBA does not read the keys for three frames, still busy, where SameBoy reads them at once, so that A is held three frames less; it parts after 29 rooms in common. The row below holds mGBA's replay of it.

# Enhanced on mGBA, continuous-transitions.route: it parts on mGBA from its recording, as the comment on its faithful rows says. Replayed to frame 6600, just before, it shows on mGBA SameBoy's figures (one vertical camera jump, no jump of Link, 79 frames waiting for a neighbour): the jumps above the row of SameBoy's are mGBA's game's, after the parting.
# continuous-transitions.route with the status bar drawn full width: the white fades, a dungeon's large rooms, and on SameBoy Subrosia's colours (mGBA's replay parts before, as above).

# neighbour-objects.route with the objects' animation stepped from the game's data against the live game (--object-animation-check), Horon's villagers, fountain and flowers: a neighbour animates an object by the rule, its code advancing its animation by one call of the step at each update of the capture's probe, and the probe's verdict is the game's on its first updates after each scroll (41 objects); of the animated, the game's changes by its data are all the step's and the step's are the game's, none wrong while Link is away; kept still by the rule, seven captured objects of several poses, among them the springbloom flowers of 0:c6 ($9c, still in their state 1 until Link touches them) and, judged on the game where no capture pairs them, Vasu's snakes ($89, set back to their animation's start each update until Link comes near), whose 178 changes by the step the game does not make (not_animated); every pose shown live has its tiles in the capture; the fountain's spurt of 0:e7 ($4c:07) is an entry or two ahead of its capture after the scroll, its code restarting its loop as Link arrives (entry_different, three captures).

# neighbour-objects.route in the far view, Horon's villagers, flowers and fountain animated in place in the rooms around: the cost of the poses' renders, under the frame's budget of the tiles' animation.
# lost-woods.route in the far view fitted to the screen (--screen): 426x320 on 1280x960, 412x360 on 1240x1080, the rules of its far 4:3 rows.
# intro.route: the night Onox's arrival puts on the troupe's camp (cutscene06Func4, from 5280 to 7032), which the neighbouring rooms take with the game's window.

# The ghost in its thread holds it as well, paced or not: the tint takes the room's palettes from its entry, delivered before the scene (dropped by the dance, its palettes kept), and needs no run during it.
# dungeon.route in the far view fitted to the screen (--screen): 426x320 on 1280x960, 412x360 on 1240x1080, the rules of its far 4:3 rows.
# dungeon.route in the view's other sizes (docs/PLAYING.md): near in 4:3, medium in 16:9 and 4:3.
# dungeon.route with the status bar drawn full width, far and near 4:3: the bands of the narrow gutters too.

# On mGBA, swim.route parts from its recording at frame 626: in the load that follows the screen turned back on, the game's logic of frame 626 ends just before the vblank on mGBA, just after it on SameBoy, and every input after is read a frame earlier; the forced swims are not reached. The row below holds mGBA's replay of it.
# Enhanced on mGBA, swim.route: it parts on mGBA from its recording, as the comment on its faithful rows says: the figures of the row below are those of mGBA's game.

# swim.route with the sub-pixel camera (--enhanced-subpixel), each core's game: where the picture switches (a scroll starting or ending, a text box opening or closing, Link drawn apart or no longer) the band's step changes by 3 px of the screen at most (enhanced.switch_band_jolt_max), where it dropped its fraction for the scroll before, up to 4 px at once; Link's by 5 at most (7 before he was drawn apart through the scrolls, where the game moves his sprites itself); his layer coming or going in a scroll no longer moves him against the ground by his own fraction, up to 3 px of the screen 61 times before (enhanced.transition_layer_shift_max).
# swim.route in far 4:3, the shape where the corners of the drawn-back band show outside the scrolls: on each core, as above.

# stairs-diagonal.route: Link up and down the stairs of 0:d9, then diagonally in 0:e9, written by hand; his sprite as the frame draws it never goes back on the screen against the step before (enhanced.link_backsteps), in every size of the view and with both camera profiles.

# stairs-diagonal.route with Link drawn in phase on a diagonal walk (--enhanced-link-phase, a trial, off by default): the stairs are left as they were; in 0:e9's diagonals the camera steps back across the walk twice instead of 12 times (enhanced.camera_wobble), and his sprite never goes back on the screen.

# stairs-diagonal.route with the sub-pixel camera (--enhanced-subpixel): at 4x the band stops between two of its steps 10 times an axis instead of 41, and steps back across the walk once instead of 12 times.

# stairs-diagonal.route with the sub-pixel camera switched off and on again six times during the walk (--enhanced-subpixel-switch), as Display's Camera from the pause: no jolt past the Pixel camera's, Link never left in the band nor drawn twice; the band's stops between its steps half way between the two cameras' (10 and 41).

# swim-hold.route: swim.route's start, Link entering the water with the flippers, then with the swim's hold (its header's option) a direction held alone, with A, then nothing; on SameBoy alone, swim.route parting on mGBA at its frame 626, before any swim.

# diagonal-crossings.route: Link crossing the edges of 0:e7, 0:e8, 0:d7 and 0:d8 diagonally in the eight ways, written by hand; with --continuous-diagonal a diagonal held carries him across the scroll's axis too (transitions.carried_frames), and the frames he stands across it two frames running (enhanced.scroll_across_stalled) are those a wall across holds him, in 0:d7's bottom row, and those whose game frame ends past the vblank, which moves nothing; every key changes between two scrolls. In the scroll from 0:e7 into 0:e8 the game draws its frame of 3355 at line 142 on SameBoy, 141 on mGBA, and its main loop waits for the vblank (wVBlankChecker) on mGBA only: from 3356 SameBoy runs a frame behind, through the same rooms entered on the same frames, its carries and walls a frame apart, which give the same counts on both but in the scroll left from 0:d8 into 0:d7: Link enters it 1.4 px higher on SameBoy (3869) than on mGBA (3871), and the carry the room's load withheld, caught up once its collisions are known, takes him to the wall of 0:d7's bottom row two frames later on SameBoy (transitions.carried_frames 292 there, 290 on mGBA). Its start is continuous-transitions.route's, whose two ghost runs into a wrong room before 0:e7 the drawn-back and sized rows forbid: the normal band only.

# diagonal-crossings.route with Link drawn in phase on a diagonal walk (--enhanced-link-phase): the camera steps back across the walk 8 times instead of 37 on SameBoy, 13 instead of 50 on mGBA; the game is the same (the transitions' counts), his sprite never goes back on the screen.

# diagonal-crossings.route with the sub-pixel camera (--enhanced-subpixel): at 4x the band stops between two of its steps 17 times an axis instead of 79 (16 on mGBA), and steps back across the walk once instead of 36 times (never instead of 54 on mGBA); the game is the same.

# shop.route: overworld.route's keys to Horon's shop (0:e6), then bombs put on B, one dropped and its blast taken, the shop entered (3:a6) and ten bombs bought for 20 rupees, written by hand.  With --cheats no-damage,rupees the blast costs no heart and the purchase nothing; with --cheats ammo the bomb is kept, and the shopkeeper, Link's bombs full, sells none.

# The compact text (--text compact, Enhanced alone), English (US) laid out (the counters of ages/checks.tsv): shop.route's price and its choice, OK or No thanks, which keep their layout, and the bombs bought.

# The text box drawn by the host (--text-box-check, the figures of ages/checks.tsv): the intro's dialogues and cutscenes, its symbols, and shop.route's price and its choice, classic and compact; the run hashes those of the rows without the check.
# intro.route with the item hotkeys' slots: the hotbar never over the opening's framed pictures (Din's scene) nor in its cutscenes (5772 frames before).
# The wide text box (--text-box wide, the counters of ages/checks.tsv), classic and compact: shop.route's price and its choice, OK or No thanks, which keep their layout, at the box's left.
# Text size Very large (--text-size xlarge, the counters of ages/checks.tsv): the wide box twice as large in Far, compact: the shop's price and its choice.
# dungeon.route with the status bar laid out: a dungeon's keys in the money's block, sixteen hearts (the tightened layout), far and near 4:3.
# continuous-transitions.route with the status bar laid out: Subrosia's ore in the money's block (on SameBoy) and the white fades.
# overworld.route with the status bar laid out in the medium view.
